bottom_line: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang quit over affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, then got his job back after pressure from President Trump. The stock shot up and is now falling again as Washington asks questions. Meanwhile the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is signaling more rate hikes, which means borrowing stays expensive.

stories.title: Nvidia's CEO drama hits Washington
stories.real: Jensen Huang resigned after reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. He was reinstated after Trump pushed for it, which added almost $1tn to Nvidia's value and lifted the Nasdaq 6.5%. Now Nvidia has dropped 7% to 9% as lawmakers demand answers and Huang heads to a DC grilling.
stories.you: Nvidia is one of the biggest companies in the market, so its swings can move the index funds in a lot of retirement accounts.

stories.title: The Fed is leaning toward more hikes
stories.real: Fed official John Williams says inflation is still too high and more rate hikes are possible 'over time.' Some analysts expect a hike in December, and investor Bill Ackman warned the Fed could trigger a recession on December 9.
stories.you: Higher rates keep car loans, credit cards and mortgages expensive, and that pressure isn't letting up yet.

stories.title: Shoppers feel better, but prices still sting
stories.real: Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 in November as the elections ended, gas prices fell and people felt better about jobs, though inflation worries are still there. Hiring sped up in October, and retailers posted strong results heading into the holidays.
stories.you: Jobs look steadier and gas is cheaper, but everyday prices are still the sore spot for most budgets.
